t: Book I: The gods in council; Athena goes to Ithaca

d: TELEMACHUS VISITS NESTOR AT PYLOS.

d: THE VISIT TO KING MENELAUS, WHO TELLS HIS STORY—MEANWHILE THE SUITORS IN ITHACA PLOT AGAINST TELEMACHUS.

t: Book V: Calypso's island; Odysseus builds his raft and is wrecked
d: CALYPSO—ULYSSES REACHES SCHERIA ON A RAFT.

t: Book VI: Nausicaa at the river of the Phaeacians
d: THE MEETING BETWEEN NAUSICAA AND ULYSSES.

t: Book VII: The palace of Alcinous
d: RECEPTION OF ULYSSES AT THE PALACE OF KING ALCINOUS.

d: BANQUET IN THE HOUSE OF ALCINOUS—THE GAMES.

t: Book IX: The Cicones, the Lotus-eaters, and the Cyclops
d: ULYSSES DECLARES HIMSELF AND BEGINS HIS STORY—-THE CICONS, LOTOPHAGI, AND CYCLOPES.

d: AEOLUS, THE LAESTRYGONES, CIRCE.

d: THE VISIT TO THE DEAD.88

d: THE SIRENS, SCYLLA AND CHARYBDIS, THE CATTLE OF THE SUN.

d: ULYSSES LEAVES SCHERIA AND RETURNS TO ITHACA.

d: ULYSSES IN THE HUT WITH EUMAEUS.

t: Book XV: Telemachus comes home from Sparta
d: MINERVA SUMMONS TELEMACHUS FROM LACEDAEMON—HE MEETS WITH THEOCLYMENUS AT PYLOS AND BRINGS HIM TO ITHACA—ON LANDING HE GOES TO THE HUT OF EUMAEUS.

d: ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO TELEMACHUS.

t: Book XVII: Odysseus enters his own house as a beggar
d: TELEMACHUS AND HIS MOTHER MEET—ULYSSES AND EUMAEUS COME DOWN TO THE TOWN, AND ULYSSES IS INSULTED BY MELANTHIUS—HE IS RECOGNISED BY THE DOG ARGOS—HE I

t: Book XVIII: The fight with Irus
d: THE FIGHT WITH IRUS—ULYSSES WARNS AMPHINOMUS—PENELOPE GETS PRESENTS FROM THE SUITORS—THE BRAZIERS—ULYSSES REBUKES EURYMACHUS.

t: Book XIX: Penelope and the stranger; the scar
d: TELEMACHUS AND ULYSSES REMOVE THE ARMOUR—ULYSSES INTERVIEWS PENELOPE—EURYCLEA WASHES HIS FEET AND RECOGNISES THE SCAR ON HIS LEG—PENELOPE TELLS HER DR

t: Book XX: Omens before the day of the bow
d: ULYSSES CANNOT SLEEP—PENELOPE’S PRAYER TO DIANA—THE TWO SIGNS FROM HEAVEN—EUMAEUS AND PHILOETIUS ARRIVE—THE SUITORS DINE—CTESIPPUS THROWS AN OX’S FOOT

t: Book XXI: The contest of the bow
d: THE TRIAL OF THE AXES, DURING WHICH ULYSSES REVEALS HIMSELF TO EUMAEUS AND PHILOETIUS

t: Book XXII: The killing of the suitors
d: THE KILLING OF THE SUITORS—THE MAIDS WHO HAVE MISCONDUCTED THEMSELVES ARE MADE TO CLEANSE THE CLOISTERS AND ARE THEN HANGED.

t: Book XXIII: Penelope knows him
d: PENELOPE EVENTUALLY RECOGNISES HER HUSBAND—EARLY IN THE MORNING ULYSSES, TELEMACHUS, EUMAEUS, AND PHILOETIUS LEAVE THE TOWN.

t: Book XXIV: Laertes, and peace in Ithaca
d: THE GHOSTS OF THE SUITORS IN HADES—ULYSSES AND HIS MEN GO TO THE HOUSE OF LAERTES—THE PEOPLE OF ITHACA COME OUT TO ATTACK ULYSSES, BUT MINERVA CONCLUD
